echo: People browse our products or add items to their cart, but leave without buying.
intro: Most stores chase abandoned carts with reminders and discounts. But people rarely leave because they forgot. **They leave because nothing convinced them this was the right product for them.** Fixing it takes two things:
t1s: the doubt that stops them at the cart
t2: Bring them back with the reason to buy
t2s: answer that doubt, not just remind them
p1_h1: GolfBays buyers wanted a simulator, but with 400+ to choose from, most browsed, stalled and left. Once the quiz told them which one was right for them, {{14 in 100 bought}} without needing a demo.
p1_context: GolfBays sells golf simulators online and was getting 440,000 Shopify sessions, but buyers couldn’t work out which simulator fit their space and needs, so they left without buying.
before_what: “Shop best sellers” and “Book a demo” buttons
after_what: A quiz built from their best sales demos
after_sub: quiz takers bought, no demo needed
built_1: Recommended the right simulator for each buyer’s space and needs, using the questions their best salespeople asked on demos
built_2: Sold the emotional payoff, such as Christmas with family in a room that used to sit empty
next1: And the ones who still leave?
p2_h1: A B2B2C audio company was sending 140,000 gamers a month to its free software, and every gamer who didn’t download straight away was [[gone for good]].
p2_context: Gamers weren’t comparing it to regular stereo sound. They were measuring it against the audio tech already inside their Dolby and Sony setups, and the site never answered the one question they had: “If this is similar to Dolby or Sony, why would I switch?”
b2_sub: no way to bring back anyone who left without downloading
a2_sub: matched gamers to their games, demoed the difference live, then followed up by email with the answer to “why switch?”
up_next: Next question: Where does most of your traffic or audience come from today?
quad: Building conviction before they buy is Speed to Decision™, and bringing back the ones who left is Compounding Revenue Per Subscriber™, quadrants 3 and 4 of the Compounding Revenue Per Visitor™ OS.
